events.title: University of Nairobi is founded
events.summary: The University of Nairobi (UoN; Swahili: Chuo Kikuu cha Nairobi) is a collegiate research university based in Nairobi and is the largest university in Kenya. Although its history as an educational institution dates back to 1956, it did not become an independent university until 1970.

events.title: GEMA is founded
events.summary: The Gikuyu, Embu, Meru, and Akamba (GEMA) is an organisation in Kenya created to presumably advance the social and political needs of the Eastern Kenya Bantu people of Gikuyu, Embu, Meru, and Akamba who though are closely related linguistically and culturally but don't have common mythologies or history. It was founded in 1971, with an economic arm, GEMA Holdings.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Gikuyu, Embu, and Meru Association

events.title: Student Organization of Nairobi University is founded
events.summary: The Student Organization of Nairobi University (abbreviated SONU) was a student movement at the University of Nairobi, Kenya. SONU was founded in 1971.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Student Organization of Nairobi University

events.title: The UN Environment Programme is established
events.summary: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is responsible for coordinating responses to environmental issues within the United Nations System. Its mandate is to provide leadership, deliver science and develop solutions on a wide range of issues, including climate change, the management of marine and terrestrial ecosystems, and green economic development.

events.title: Joe (magazine) is founded
events.summary: Joe was a magazine published in Kenya between 1973 and 1979, at the height of what publisher Henry Chakava described as the "fat years" of Kenyan publishing. Joe was one of several publications aimed at the new urban middle and lower-middle classes, and used subversive humour, art and fiction as a medium for cultural, social and political analysis.

events.title: Lokiriama Peace Accord
events.summary: The Lokiriama Peace Accord is a peace treaty between the Turkana people of Kenya and the Matheniko of Uganda signed in December 1973 as a commitment by both parties to peacefully co-exist. The accord derives its name from Lokiriama, a remote town in Turkana District, North Western Kenya that is inhabited by the Turkana.

events.title: Sibiloi National Park is established
events.summary: Sibiloi National Park lies on the northeastern shore of Lake Turkana in northern Kenya. Established in 1973 by the government of Kenya for the protection of wildlife and paleontologist sites.

events.title: The Kenyatta International Conference Centre opens
events.summary: The Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC), formerly the Kenyatta International Conference Centre, is a 32-story building located in Nairobi, Kenya. The KICC is located in the City Square of Nairobi, and is a crucial address for a number of Government offices, including those of recently elected Senators.

events.title: Saiwa Swamp National Park is established
events.summary: Saiwa Swamp National Park is located near Kitale, in Trans-Nzoia County, Rift Valley Province, Kenya. It is the smallest national park in Kenya, only 3 km2 (1.2 sq mi), and was created as a habitat for the Sitatunga, a rare aquatic antelope.

events.title: Shaba National Reserve is established
events.summary: Shaba National Reserve is a protected area in Isiolo County in northern Kenya to the east of the Samburu and Buffalo Springs national reserves. Together, the three reserves form a large protected area.

events.title: 1974 Kenyan general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Kenya on 14 October 1974. At the time, the country was a de facto one-party state with the Kenya African National Union being the sole party to participate in the election.

events.title: Lufthansa Flight 540
events.summary: Lufthansa Flight 540 was a scheduled commercial flight for Lufthansa, serving the Frankfurt–Nairobi–Johannesburg route. On 20 November 1974, the Boeing 747-130 that was operating as Flight 540 was carrying 157 people (139 passengers and 18 crew members) crashed and caught fire shortly after taking off from Embakasi Airport in Nairobi, Kenya, for the last leg of the flight, resulting in the deaths of 54 passengers and 5 crew members.

events.title: KNM ER 3733 is found
events.summary: KNM ER 3733 is a fossilized hominid cranium of the extinct hominid Homo ergaster, alternatively referred to as African Homo erectus. It was discovered in 1975 in Koobi Fora, Kenya, right next to Lake Turkana, in a survey led by Richard Leakey, by a field worker called Bernard Ngeneo.

events.title: Nakuru Agreement
events.summary: The Nakuru Agreement, signed on June 21, 1975, in Nakuru, Kenya, was an attempt to salvage the January 15 1975 Alvor Agreement, which granted Angola independence from Portugal and established a transitional government. While the Nakuru Agreement did produce a short truce between the three nationalist movements—the Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA), National Liberation Front of Angola (FNLA), and National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA)— clashes resumes on July 9, 1975.

events.title: 1975 Nairobi bus bombing
events.summary: On 1 March 1975, a bomb exploded on a crowded bus in central Nairobi in Kenya. It killed at least 27 people and injured another 90 when it detonated, ripping the bus open.

events.title: Boni National Reserve is established
events.summary: The Boni National Reserve is a national reserve for conservation and lies in the Garissa County, Kenya. The reserve covers an area of 1,339 km2 (517 sq mi) and is managed by Kenya Wildlife Service.

events.title: Mwea National Reserve is established
events.summary: The Mwea National Reserve is a Kenyan national reserve located south of Embu. Its altitude ranges between 1,000 and 1,100 m (3,300 and 3,600 ft), dominated by the Acacia-Commiphora bushland on the north shore of Kamburu Reservoir, at the confluence of Tana and Thiba Rivers.

events.title: The Green Belt Movement is founded
events.summary: The Green Belt Movement (GBM) is an indigenous grassroots organization in Kenya that empowers women through the planting of trees. It is one of the most effective and well-known grassroots organisations addressing the problem of global deforestation.

events.title: The Sheldrick Wildlife Trust is founded
events.summary: The Sheldrick Wildlife Trust (SWT) operates an orphaned elephant rescue and wildlife rehabilitation program in Nairobi, Kenya. It was founded in 1977 by Dame Daphne Sheldrick to honour her late husband, David.

events.title: Kisite-Mpunguti Marine National Park is established
events.summary: Kisite-Mpunguti Marine National Park was established in 1978 by the Kenyan government and it is Kenya's first Blue Park. Kisite is situated on the southern coast of Kenya near Shimoni and south of Wasini Island in Kwale County near the Tanzanian border.

events.title: The Kenya Ports Authority is established
events.summary: Kenya Ports Authority (KPA) is a state corporation with the responsibility to "maintain, operate, improve and regulate all scheduled seaports" on the Indian Ocean coastline of Kenya, including principally Kilindini Harbour at Mombasa. Other KPA ports include Lamu, Malindi, Kilifi, Mtwapa, Kiunga, Shimoni, Funzi and Vanga.

events.title: UN-Habitat is established
events.summary: The United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is the United Nations programme for human settlements and sustainable urban development. It was established in 1977 as an outcome of the first United Nations Conference on Human Settlements and Sustainable Urban Development (Habitat I) held in Vancouver, Canada, in 1976.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: United Nations Human Settlements Programme

events.title: Daniel arap Moi becomes president
events.summary: The presidency of Daniel arap Moi began on 22 August 1978, when Daniel arap Moi was sworn in as the 2nd President of Kenya, and ended on 30 December 2002. Moi, a KANU party member, took office following the death of the then president Jomo Kenyatta on the same day.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Presidency of Daniel arap Moi

events.title: 1978 Kenyan presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Kenya on 8 November 1978, the first not to be held concurrently with parliamentary elections. They followed the death in office of President Jomo Kenyatta in August 1978.

events.title: Kiunga Marine National Reserve is established
events.summary: Kiunga Marine National Reserve is situated along the Indian Ocean coast of Lamu District, Coast Province, Kenya. Kiunga park covers 270 square kilometres (100 sq mi).

events.title: 1979 Kenyan general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Kenya on 8 November 1979. At the time, the country was a de facto one-party state with the Kenya African National Union being the sole party to participate in the election.
